outcomes.text: Define and calculate specific heat capacity.
Suggest experiments to measure specific heat capacity.
Analyse everyday effects of water's large specific heat.
Use the terms for changes of state between solid, liquid and gas.
Explain thermal expansion with kinetic theory.
Analyse applications and consequences of thermal expansion.
Analyse melting, solidification, boiling and condensation using particles.
State melting and boiling temperatures of water at standard pressure.
Describe expansion of solids qualitatively.
Explain expansion of liquids, real and apparent.
Explain gas pressure in terms of particle collisions.
Differentiate boiling from evaporation.
Describe evaporation as escape of energetic particles.
Analyse how temperature, humidity, area and air movement affect evaporation.
Explain how evaporation causes cooling.
Describe evaporative cooling in refrigeration.
Explain latent heat using particle behaviour.
Justify experiments to find latent heat of fusion and vaporisation.
State that some materials become superconducting near absolute zero.
Describe superconductivity.
Justify experiments separating good and bad thermal conductors.
Explain conduction in solids by lattice vibrations and free electrons.
Explain convection in fluids through density changes.
Explain convection in seawater supporting marine life.
Describe land and sea breezes.
Explain how birds and gliders use thermals.
Describe heat transfer by radiation, needing no medium.
Describe how surface colour and texture affect infrared emission and absorption.
Justify how emission depends on temperature and area.
Justify experiments on good and bad emitters and absorbers.
Analyse the greenhouse effect as a result of heat radiation.
Analyse everyday uses of conduction, convection and radiation.

units.title: Domain D: Waves, Sound and Light

outcomes.text: Show that waves transfer energy without moving matter.
Describe wave motion.
Describe wave features: wavefront, crest and trough.
Define frequency, wavelength and amplitude.
Use wave speed = frequency x wavelength.
Illustrate transverse waves.
Illustrate longitudinal waves.
Describe reflection, refraction and diffraction of waves.
Describe how wavelength affects diffraction at an edge.
Analyse tsunamis as shallow-water waves.
Describe how wavelength and gap size affect diffraction.
Describe how sound is produced.
Describe sound as a longitudinal wave.
State the audible frequency range for humans.
Justify why sound cannot travel in a vacuum.
Describe how amplitude and frequency change loudness and pitch.
Describe how different sources produce different waveforms.
Describe an echo as reflected sound.
Justify experiments showing reflection of sound.
Illustrate a method to measure the speed of sound.
State that sound in air travels about 330-350 m/s.
Describe how sound speed differs in solids, liquids and gases.
Define ultrasound as sound above 20 kHz.
Illustrate and analyse uses of ultrasound.
Illustrate the use of infrasound.
Analyse effects of noise pollution.
Justify the importance of acoustic protection.
Describe how sound properties are used in applications.
Explain how soft materials reduce echo.
Explain with examples how sound reflects, refracts and diffracts.
Explain how the ear converts sound into nerve signals.
Define normal, angle of incidence and angle of reflection.
Describe an experiment to find the position and nature of a mirror image.
Use the laws of reflection in simple optics problems.
Define normal, angle of incidence and refraction.
Explain that a wave refracts toward the normal on entering a slower medium.
Define and use refractive index from vacuum to a medium.
Define n = sin i / sin r and apply Snell's law.
Describe an experiment showing refraction through a block.
Define critical angle and total internal reflection.
Derive n = 1/sin c.
Apply n = 1/sin c to problems.
Describe experiments showing total internal reflection.
Evaluate the use of optical fibres.
Analyse thin converging and diverging lenses.
Define focal length, principal axis and principal focus.
Draw ray diagrams for real and virtual images.
Differentiate real from virtual images.
Define and calculate linear magnification.
Describe a single lens as a magnifying glass.
Describe single lenses in optical devices.
Draw ray diagrams for image formation in optical devices.
Describe lenses correcting eye defects.
Explain dispersion of light by a prism.
State the seven colours of the visible spectrum in order.
Illustrate how the eye processes colour.
State that extreme gravity from objects like black holes bends light.
State that acoustic lenses focus sound using shape and material.

units.title: Domain E: Electricity, Magnetism and Electronics

outcomes.text: State that there are positive and negative charges.
State that like charges repel and unlike attract.
Describe experiments on charging by friction.
Explain that friction charging moves only electrons.
Explain how an insulator is discharged.
Explain charging a conductor by induction.
Describe where charging causes problems.
Suggest how charging and discharging are used.
Describe an electric field as a region where charge feels force.
State that field direction is the force on a positive charge.
Analyse and draw simple field patterns.
State examples of conductors and insulators.
Describe an experiment to tell conductors from insulators.
Use a simple electron model for conductors and insulators.
Explain how a lightning rod protects people.
Explain electrical breakdown.
State that corona discharge and Lichtenberg figures are visible discharges.
Explain how lightning forms.
State that there are many kinds of lightning.
Define and calculate electric current.
Explain conduction in metals by electron flow.
State that current is measured in amperes.
Differentiate d.c. from a.c.
Differentiate conventional from actual current.
Justify and show the use of ammeters.
Define e.m.f.
Define potential difference.
State that e.m.f. and p.d. are measured in volts.
Justify and show the use of voltmeters.
Calculate total e.m.f. of cells in series.
State the e.m.f. of identical cells in parallel.
Describe an experiment to find resistance.
Define and calculate resistivity.
Define and apply Ohm's law.
Describe how temperature changes resistance.
Interpret current-voltage graphs.
Draw circuit diagrams.
Use current and voltage rules for series and parallel circuits.
Calculate combined resistance in series.
Calculate combined resistance of two resistors in parallel.
Calculate current, voltage and resistance in circuit parts.
Describe the action of an NTC thermistor.
Analyse variable potential dividers.
Justify and show the use of resistor colour codes.
Describe the working of a diode.
Describe how an LED passes current.
Describe how relays switch circuits.
State common uses of electricity.
Justify connecting lamps in parallel.
Use P = IV.
Use E = IVt.
Define the kilowatt-hour.
Explain choosing components with suitable power ratings.
Calculate the cost of using electrical appliances.
State common electrical hazards.
Explain trip switches and fuses.
Explain what happens when a live wire touches a metal case.
Explain why metal casings must be earthed.
State that a mains circuit has live, neutral and earth wires.
Explain why fuses and breakers are on the live wire.
Explain why domestic supplies are parallel.
Explain the damage electric shock does to the body.
Explain that electronic devices are built from digital logic.
Explain that Boolean logic underlies analogue-to-digital conversion.
State logic gate actions in words and truth tables.
Identify logic gates in security uses.
Use circuit symbols for logic gates.
Identify how Boolean switches combine in problems.
Describe an npn transistor as a switch.
Explain that transistors are used in digital devices.
State that some circuits keep their state after an input.
State that quantum computers are early in development.
Compare analogue and digital electronics.
Describe an experiment showing electromagnetic induction.
Use factors that affect induced e.m.f.
Use Lenz's law for the effect of induced current.
Describe how a.c. generators work.
Sketch and interpret e.m.f.-time graphs for a.c.
Describe the magnetic field pattern around a current-carrying conductor.
State how field changes with current and direction.
Describe the magnetic effect of current in relays.
Describe an experiment showing a force on a current in a field.
State and use the relative directions of force, field and current.
Describe field patterns between parallel currents.
State that a current-carrying coil in a field can turn.
Describe the operation of an electric motor.
State that Earth's magnetic field is thought to come from molten iron movement.
Explain how a simple iron-cored transformer works.
Use primary, secondary, step-up and step-down.
Use Vp/Vs = Np/Ns.
Justify the advantages of high-voltage transmission.
Describe electron beam deflection by electric and magnetic fields.
Interpret oscilloscope waveforms.
State the regions of the electromagnetic spectrum in order.
State that all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in vacuum.
Describe applications of electromagnetic waves.
Describe damage caused by electromagnetic radiation.
Explain qualitatively how light scattering gives the blue sky.
State that light can be treated as photons carrying momentum.
Describe the structure of the atom.
Justify the findings of alpha scattering experiments.
Define proton number and nucleon number.
Use nuclide notation.
Explain isotopes.
Explain background radiation.
State the main sources of background radiation.
Describe radiation emission as spontaneous and random.
Describe alpha, beta and gamma radiation.
Justify the order of ionising and penetrating power of radiations.
Describe deflection of radiation in electric and magnetic fields.
Explain radioactive decay as a change in an unstable nucleus.
Use decay equations with nuclide notation.
Recognise that matter can be converted to energy and the reverse.
Use E = mc^2 to calculate energy released.
Describe activity of a radioactive material in counts per second.
Define and infer half-life.
Explain and apply carbon dating.
Explain how radiation type and half-life determine uses.
State the effects of ionising radiation on living things.
Explain how radioactive materials are moved, used and stored safely.
Explain the nature of the Sun as a medium-sized star.
Describe the hypothesis that most matter in the universe is dark matter.
Explain how global warming contributes to extreme weather.
Explain geothermal activity.
Explain with examples that a scientific idea must be falsifiable.
Explain with examples how lab hazards can be reduced.
Identify risks in a given experimental procedure.
Identify the meaning of common hazard signs.
Call emergency services after a lab accident.
Define true value, error, accuracy, precision and related terms.
Identify apparatus for collecting data.
Plan how data will be tabulated or graphed.
Explain step by step how data will be analysed.
Suggest how human and systematic errors can be reduced.
Set up apparatus under supervision.
Avoid parallax error.
Identify and correct zero error.
Take enough readings to average out random error.
Take correct meniscus readings.
Record sources of potential error.
Avoid systematic error in the specific experiment.
Make measurements with common laboratory apparatus.
Use a stopwatch to time intervals, including oscillations.
Use analogue scales and digital displays.
Measure physical quantities such as length, volume and mass.
Measure small distances or short time intervals.
Determine a derived quantity such as extension per unit load.
Test the relationship between two variables.
Compare measured quantities such as angles of reflection.
Compare derived quantities such as density.
Heat and cool materials and measure temperature.
Run experiments with springs and balances.
Time motion or oscillations.
Work with electric circuits, connecting and reconnecting.
Do optics experiments with pins and transparent, translucent and opaque materials.
Use procedures with simple apparatus in other situations.
Record measured and calculated quantities with correct units.
Organise tabulated results with headings and units.
Label graph axes with quantities and units.
Choose scales that use most of the graph paper.
Plot points accurately.
Plot points with small crosses or fine dots.
Use measuring instruments to full precision.
Estimate significant figures for calculated quantities.
Show clear working in calculations.
Express ratios as decimals to sensible figures.
Sketch lines of best fit with balanced points.
Calculate the gradient of a straight line from a graph.
Determine the intercept of a straight-line graph.
Take readings from graphs by extrapolation.
Identify whether a procedure is valid.
Identify whether a procedure is reliable.
Recommend how to reduce random and systematic errors.
Identify unsafe steps in an experimental design.
